niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “best” CTV advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, target markets, and whether you need programmatic scale, premium inventory buys, creative production, or performance ROI. I can shortlist agencies once you tell me more about what you need. Below are practical criteria, the common types of top partners, examples, and next steps to find the best fit.

What to consider when choosing a CTV agency
- Primary goal: brand awareness vs performance (sales, installs, leads).  
- Scale & geography: global vs local/country-specific buys.  
- Inventory access: direct relationships with Roku/Hulu/YouTube/streamers vs programmatic DSP access.  
- Data & targeting: household-level targeting, use of first/third-party data, identity resolution.  
- Measurement & attribution: viewability, GRPs, incremental reach, conversion tracking, MMM or experiments.  
- Creative capability: 6–30s CTV creative, dynamic creative, sequential storytelling.  
- Transparency & fees: media transparency, platform fees, reporting cadence.  
- Privacy & compliance: support for cookieless/ID-less environments and CCPA/GDPR compliance.

Types of partners and examples
- Global holding-group agencies (good for large, cross-market brand campaigns and premium inventory): examples include Mindshare, Wavemaker, MediaCom (WPP); OMD, PHD (Omnicom); Starcom, Zenith (Publicis); Carat, iProspect, Merkle (Dentsu); Initiative, UM (IPG); Havas Media.  
- Programmatic / performance specialists (good for targeting, optimization, ROI focus): often work closely with DSPs (The Trade Desk) and have deep CTV programmatic expertise. Boutique performance shops (e.g., Tinuiti, 3Q Digital) also run CTV for direct-response advertisers.  
- Platform/streamer solutions (ideal if you want native buys on a single platform): Roku OneView, Amazon/Fire TV Ads, Hulu/Disney/Peacock direct ad teams — these are not full-service agencies but excellent for platform-native reach.  
- Independent CTV specialists / consultancies: smaller agencies focused on CTV/OTT strategy, measurement and creative. Good when you want nimble, highly technical execution or tailored pilots.

How to evaluate finalists
- Ask for CTV-specific case studies and KPIs (reach, completion rates, conversions, CPMs).  
- Request transparency on inventory sources and whether buys are direct or programmatic.  
- Check measurement tools and third-party verification partners (Nielsen, IAS, Moat, Comscore).  
- Run a short pilot (4–8 weeks) with clear KPIs before committing long-term.  
- Confirm creative production capabilities for CTV specs and dynamic creative.  
- Clarify reporting cadence, ownership of data, and post-campaign learnings.

If you want, I can:
- Shortlist 3–5 agencies tailored to your needs (tell me: country/markets, monthly media budget, main KPI, and whether you want programmatic vs direct buys).  
- Draft a short RFP/template of questions to send to agencies.  
Which would you prefer?
